items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: then a few weeks later, made another with Clark Terry, Count Basie, Lockjaw Davis

ctx.x: Yes, he played a chorus, I played a chorus on trumpet, Clark Terry, Claude Perry, Dizzy Gillespie, John Faddis, and ... is that 6? Dizzy Gillespie, Claude Perry, Clark Terry, Doc Cheatham, Faddis, Carter -- Faddis, Carter -- who was the other one? There was another one -- there were 6 of us. Harry Edison.

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’s the most gentlemanly gentleman you’ll ever meet in your life. He’s a marvelous person. We call him “the King,” because he’s the boss at doing everything, playing trumpet, playing alto, playing trombone, piano, arranging, composing, and movie scores and all. He’s a very talented man.

ctx.x: The thing about him is he – every experience I’ve had with him, he’s the ultimate gentleman.
